gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 10 build step is the narrowest honest place to keep the virtio_input survey reviewable alongside the already-landed helper and the focused status-drain replay.
The existing virtio core lab slice already covers status and queue bookkeeping, so the virtio_input lane can rely on that footing instead of reopening core-side work.
The live repo already has a bounded in-memory ring helper for queue shape and notification bookkeeping, which is the minimum queue-facing support the virtio_input starter depends on.

The first virtio_input-specific helper is already landed and now models identity snapshots, config bitmaps, ABS metadata, queue planning, ready-state gating, and multitouch timestamp suppression without claiming transport parity.
Dedicated Phase 10 tests already keep the starter helper honest around capped string copies, queue planning, ready gating, reset behavior, and MSC_TIMESTAMP suppression.
The slice note already records what the landed helper covers so the survey can focus on the remaining roadmap gap rather than re-explaining the starter surface.
A dedicated survey gate keeps the current virtio_input roadmap gap explicit now that the repo already has a starter helper and test path.

The lane needs a Phase 10 note that compares the live starter against the roadmap, states the current lab-only driver validation evidence plainly, and prevents the repo from overstating input-driver progress.

The live repo now includes one bounded in-memory capability-setup helper that connects `virtinput_cfg_bits()`, `virtinput_cfg_abs()`, `input_set_capability()`, and `input_set_abs_params()` intent without claiming transport-backed config reads or input-core registration.

The live repo now includes one bounded in-memory multitouch slot-planning helper keyed off `ABS_MT_SLOT`, which gives the lab slice a truthful slot-count foothold before any `input_register_device()` or transport-backed queue work.

The live repo now includes one bounded registration-preflight summary that reports queue, ready-state, capability-setup, and multitouch-slot blockers before any future `input_register_device()` handoff, which keeps the remaining lifecycle gap explicit without claiming transport-backed parity.

The live repo now includes one bounded queue-callback preflight summary that reports event and status queue configuration, event-buffer fill state, and ready-state blockers before any future transport-backed callback handoff.

The live repo now includes one bounded in-memory status-drain helper that mirrors the `virtinput_recv_status()` reclaim step closely enough to retire completed status sends from the lab queue model without claiming transport-backed callbacks.

Real event delivery, `input_register_device()` lifecycle coverage, freeze or restore behavior, and transport-backed queue callbacks remain too risky even after the registration-preflight, queue-callback preflight, multitouch slot, and status-drain helpers landed, until broader queue callback plumbing is in place.
